meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: That means this man is a sly swindler!

examples.text: Значит, ваш сегодняшний ужин не отменяется.
examples.trans: So your dinner tonight is not canceled.
What do you mean, as another person?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Thank you for your answer.
Your courage is worthy of great admiration.
Your business is postponed for a little while.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодняшний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('today's').

examples.text: Значит, ваш сегодняшний ужин не отменяется.
examples.trans: So your dinner tonight is not canceled.
What is today's menu?
The main ingredient of today's contest is cod!

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'dinner, supper (evening meal)' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You deserved this star, after all!

examples.text: Значит, ваш сегодняшний ужин не отменяется.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Без меня вы звезду не получите.
examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: А Елена Павловна разве не против?
examples.trans: And is Elena Pavlovna not against it?
No, she is not against it at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'меняться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'is canceled', paired with 'отмениться'.

examples.trans: The truth is canceled.

examples.text: С этого момента вся правда отменяется!
examples.trans: From this moment on, all truth is canceled!
The exhibition is cancelled.

examples.trans: Without me you will never get a star.

examples.text: На два часа я её уговорил.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'сьба'). Common feminine noun meaning 'a request' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Виктор, у меня к вам просьба.

examples.text: У меня к тебе маленькая просьба.

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'зможно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Perhaps it will seem strange to you.

examples.text: Возможно, вы любите есть сырую рыбу.
examples.trans: Perhaps, you like to eat raw fish.

examples.text: Как это сегодня вечером? Это невозможно!
examples.trans: What do you mean, this evening? That's impossible!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'she', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: No, she is not against it at all.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'казаться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to seem, appear', paired with 'казаться'.

examples.text: Тебе показалось, она смотрела на всех.
examples.trans: You imagined it, she was looking at everyone.
I wanted to show it to the local policeman.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'транный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('strange').

examples.trans: Perhaps it will seem strange to you.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'want', paired with 'захотеть'.
